tour.overview:
Long before classical Athens, the Mycenaeans ruled Greece from fortified palaces in the Peloponnese. Homer called their capital 'Mycenae, rich in gold', and its king, Agamemnon, led the Greeks against Troy. Their citadel, with its massive walls and Lion Gate, and their beehive tombs still stand in the hills of the Argolid. Nearby, the sanctuary of Asclepius at Epidaurus was the most famous healing centre of the ancient world, and its theatre, built in the 4th century BC, is still used for performances. Mycenae and Epidaurus are both UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

This private day crosses the Corinth Canal into the Peloponnese with a licensed archaeologist guide. You explore Mycenae in the morning, have lunch in the elegant Venetian town of Nafplio by the sea, and end at Epidaurus, where you can test the acoustics by whispering on the stage while your companions listen from the top row.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 11 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Athens
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate; about 5 km on uneven ground, with a climb in Mycenae

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Corinth Canal.
• Mycenae: the Lion Gate, Grave Circle A, the palace and the museum.
• The Treasury of Atreus.
• Nafplio: the old town, Syntagma Square and the harbour with the Bourtzi.
• Epidaurus: the theatre and the sanctuary of Asclepius.

WHY THIS WORKS
Three great sites in one region, about an hour apart; with a car and driver the day is easy and we can take the scenic coast road back.

WHO IT SUITS
History and mythology lovers, theatre lovers and anyone who has seen Athens and wants to discover the Peloponnese.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer a shorter day, choose Delphi or Cape Sounion. With more time, spend a night in Nafplio and add Ancient Olympia.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The sites are exposed and hot in summer: bring a hat and water. In July and August the Athens Epidaurus Festival performs ancient plays in the theatre on Friday and Saturday evenings; ask us if you want tickets.

days.name: The Corinth Canal, Mycenae and the Treasury of Atreus, lunch in Nafplio and the theatre of Epidaurus
days.description:
What to expect: the Bronze Age kingdom of Agamemnon, a Venetian seaside town and the best-preserved theatre of antiquity, with a licensed guide, private car, tickets and lunch.

Your driver collects you at your hotel at about 7:30 and drives west along the coast to the Corinth Canal, about an hour away. You walk onto the bridge and look straight down 80 metres to the water: the canal, 6.4 kilometres long and only 25 metres wide, was cut through solid rock between 1881 and 1893, realising a dream of Greek and Roman rulers since Periander and Nero.

You continue into the Argolid to Mycenae. Your guide leads you through the Lion Gate, built around 1250 BC, its two carved lions the oldest monumental sculpture in Europe, framed by walls of boulders so huge that later Greeks believed only the Cyclopes could have moved them. Inside, you see Grave Circle A, where Heinrich Schliemann found the gold death masks in 1876 – one he believed was the face of Agamemnon – climb to the palace on the summit and see the secret cistern tunnel. In the museum you see finds from the site, and below the citadel you enter the Treasury of Atreus, a beehive tomb whose corbelled dome, 13 metres high, was the largest in the world for over a thousand years.

Lunch is in Nafplio, 30 minutes away, the first capital of independent Greece from 1829 to 1834. Its old town of Venetian and neoclassical houses, bougainvillea and marble-paved squares sits below the Palamidi fortress, and the little Bourtzi castle stands on an islet in the harbour. After lunch at a taverna and time for a gelato on the waterfront, you drive to Epidaurus.

The theatre of Epidaurus, built in the late 4th century BC with 55 rows for some 13,000 spectators, is famous for its acoustics: a coin dropped or a match struck in the centre of the stage can be heard in the top row. You try it yourselves, then walk through the sanctuary of Asclepius, god of medicine, where patients slept in the hope of a healing dream. You drive back to Athens, arriving at about 18:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:30 – Pick-up at your hotel in Athens.
08:30 – Corinth Canal.
09:45 – Mycenae and the Treasury of Atreus (about 2 hours).
12:15 – Nafplio: lunch and free time.
14:45 – Epidaurus (about 1 hour 30 minutes).
16:30 – Drive back to Athens.
18:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The Palamidi fortress (999 steps, or by car) can be added in Nafplio.
• Ancient Corinth can replace the canal stop.
• Summer festival performances at Epidaurus can be combined with a night in Nafplio.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Mycenae and Epidaurus tickets, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: Palamidi fortress, drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is it a long day?
faq.answer: About 11 hours, with roughly 5 hours of driving in short stretches. If you can, spend a night in Nafplio and make it two relaxed days.

faq.question: Are the entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: Mycenae (including the Treasury of Atreus and the museum) and Epidaurus (theatre, sanctuary and museum).

faq.question: Can we really hear a whisper at Epidaurus?
faq.answer: Yes. On a quiet day, a coin dropped or a page torn in the centre of the stage can be heard in the top rows. Your guide shows you where to stand.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, lunch at a taverna in Nafplio. Vegetarian and other diets can be arranged.

faq.question: Is there much walking?
faq.answer: About 5 km on uneven ground. Mycenae has a climb to the palace and steep steps into the cistern, which you can skip.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the lions, the giant walls and testing the acoustics. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Epidaurus has a ramp to the lower part of the theatre; Mycenae is steep and rocky. The canal and Nafplio are easy.

faq.question: Can we see a play at Epidaurus?
faq.answer: In July and August, the festival stages ancient plays on Friday and Saturday evenings. We can book tickets and a night in Nafplio.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes with grip, a hat and sun cream. The sites have little shade.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: March to June and September to November. Summer is hot; we start early. Spring brings wild flowers to the ruins.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
